newsitem.title: JAPAN: Asia Metals -- Japan coasts into fiscal year-end.
newsitem.headline: Asia Metals -- Japan coasts into fiscal year-end.

text.p: Japanese metal markets were quiet over the past week, as traders and end-users prepared to close their books at the end of the fiscal year on March 31, traders said.
The steady slide in the yen against the dollar was also discouraging consumers from stepping into the market.

In the aluminium market, traders said end users continued buying mainly on a hand-to-mouth basis, showing little interest in entering the market on Tuesday when London Metal Exchange prices slipped below $1,650 a tonne to a one-week low.

One trader said that, although Japanese end users had been tending to buy modestly on price dips, LME aluminium's recent inability to make a sustained move through resistance in the $1,670 to $1,700 range had fuelled expectations that prices were set to dip further.
He added that few Japanese end users had made any purchases for the second half of this calendar year.
Aluminium premiums remained firm, held up by strength in U.S. premiums.
The copper market was expected to remain quiet at least through May, with near-term needs likely to be covered by imports under Japan's general system of preference (GSP) scheme.

Traders estimated that buying related to the GSP, which grants a tariff exemption to developing country imports submitted for customs clearance at the beginning of the fiscal year, was light this year at 50,000 tonnes or less.

Japan's copper demand was expected to be lacklustre in 1997/98. On Wednesday two key end user organisations, representing Japan's cable and brass makers, predicted that demand in 1997/98 for their output would rise a marginal 0.1 percent to 0.2 percent.
